## Project Overview

Mocha is an open-source, general-purpose JavaScript testing framework designed for Node.js and browser environments. [PROJECT_CHARTER.md:9-12][package.json]  
The repository contains the Mocha runtime, command-line interface, browser bundle source, reporters, interfaces, plugins, documentation site, and test suites. [lib/mocha.cjs:168-188][lib/cli/cli.js:80-97][browser-entry.js:90-100][docs/README.md:1-6]  
The main technologies visible are Node.js, JavaScript, TypeScript declarations and checking, Rollup, Playwright, Webpack, and Astro Starlight. [package.json][tsconfig.json][docs/README.md:1-6][docs/package.json]  
Likely runtime entry points include `bin/mocha.js` for the CLI, `lib/mocha.cjs` for the core Mocha API, and `browser-entry.js` for browser usage. [bin/mocha.js:41-46][lib/mocha.cjs:168-188][browser-entry.js:90-100]  
The package identifies itself as Mocha version `12.0.2` and describes itself as a testing framework for Node.js and the browser. [package.json]

## Setup / Installation

Use Node.js `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`; Node.js 22 LTS is recommended. [AGENTS.md:22-27][.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:6-12]  
Use npm for this repository; yarn and pnpm are explicitly unsupported. [AGENTS.md:22-27][.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:6-12]  
Install Google Chrome if you intend to run browser tests locally. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:6-12]  
Clone or fork the repository, then run `npm install` from the repository root. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:13-19]  
Optional dependencies may fail during installation; those failures can generally be ignored unless you are building the documentation. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:13-19]  
For a script-free installation, use `npm install --ignore-scripts`. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:13-19]  
For a clean CI-style installation, the repository guidance recommends `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. [AGENTS.md:47-53]  
Documentation work uses a separate package under `docs/`; install its dependencies with `cd docs && npm install`. [AGENTS.md:47-53][docs/README.md:7-17]  
The supplied setup instructions do not identify a required repository-level environment variable. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:13-19][AGENTS.md:47-53]

## Running Locally

Run `npm test` to execute the repository’s full validation command, including linting and Node.js and browser testing. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-34]  
Useful focused commands include `npm run test-smoke`, `npm run test-node:unit`, `npm run test-node:integration`, `npm run test-node:interfaces`, `npm run test-node:reporters`, `npm run test-browser`, `npm run tsc`, and `npm run lint`. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:35-47]  
For a watch-mode development cycle, run `npx mocha --watch test/unit/`. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:48-53]  
Build the generated browser bundle with `npm run clean` followed by `npm run build`; the build uses Rollup. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:55-65][package.json]  
The `test-browser` script itself cleans, builds, and runs browser tests, so it is the safer browser-development command. [package.json][AGENTS.md:87-92]  
The documentation site can be developed with `cd docs`, `npm i`, `npm run generate`, and `npm run dev`. [docs/README.md:7-17]  
The documentation package also exposes `npm run start` as an alias for its Astro development server. [docs/package.json]  
The supplied evidence does not specify a fixed local port for either the main project or the documentation server. [docs/README.md:7-17][docs/package.json]  
Do not edit `mocha.js` or `mocha.js.map` directly because they are generated bundle artifacts. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:55-65][AGENTS.md:37-42]

## Project Structure

`bin/` contains the command-line entry point, including `bin/mocha.js`. [bin/mocha.js:41-46]  
`lib/` contains the primary implementation, including the Mocha class, CLI modules, Node.js utilities, runners, suites, tests, hooks, plugins, reporters, and type declarations. [lib/mocha.cjs:168-188][lib/cli/cli.js:80-97][lib/nodejs/buffered-worker-pool.cjs:85-93][lib/plugin-loader.js:39-48][lib/types.d.ts:19-26]  
`lib/cli/` handles argument parsing, configuration, file lookup, run preparation, and watch mode. [lib/cli/options.cjs:42-67][lib/cli/lookup-files.js:32-32][lib/cli/run.cjs:125-131][lib/cli/watch-run.cjs:444-488]  
`lib/reporters/` contains built-in reporter implementations such as HTML, JSON, JSON stream, TAP, Spec, and XUnit reporters. [lib/reporters/html.js:58-88][lib/reporters/json.js:108-123][lib/reporters/json-stream.js:66-87][lib/reporters/tap.js:150-185][lib/reporters/xunit.js:119-148]  
`test/` is organized into smoke tests, unit tests, integration tests, interface tests, reporter tests, browser-specific tests, compiler fixtures, plugin fixtures, and supporting fixtures and helpers. [test/smoke/smoke.spec.cjs:12-14][test/unit/context.spec.cjs:6-13][test/integration/config.spec.cjs:30-32][test/interfaces/bdd.spec.js:25-27][test/reporters/base.spec.cjs:50-52][test/browser-specific/esm.spec.js:7-9]  
`docs/` is a separate Astro Starlight documentation package with its own package metadata, TypeScript configuration, content, and development scripts. [docs/README.md:1-6][docs/package.json][docs/tsconfig.json]  
`example/config/` contains illustrative Node.js configuration examples rather than project boilerplates. [example/config/README.md:1-7]  
`repro/` is an optional, separate minimal Node.js project for reproducing end-user behavior against the local checkout. [repro/README.md:1-9][repro/README.md:12-35]

## Testing

The repository tests Mocha itself with Mocha’s own test runner and npm scripts. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-47][package.json]  
The main validation command is `npm test`. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-34]  
Smoke tests are located under `test/smoke/`, including `test/smoke/smoke.spec.cjs`. [test/smoke/smoke.spec.cjs:12-14]  
Unit tests are located under `test/unit/`, with suites covering context, errors, hooks, Mocha instances, runners, suites, utilities, and related components. [test/unit/context.spec.cjs:6-13][test/unit/errors.spec.cjs:9-11][test/unit/runner.spec.cjs:28-30][test/unit/suite.spec.cjs:12-14]  
Integration tests are located under `test/integration/`, with option, plugin, regression, helper, and fixture areas. [test/integration/config.spec.cjs:30-32][test/integration/options/watch.spec.cjs:38-40][test/integration/plugins/global-fixtures.spec.cjs:148-152][test/integration/helpers.cjs:851-855]  
Reporter tests are located under `test/reporters/`, and browser-specific tests are located under `test/browser-specific/`. [test/reporters/base.spec.cjs:50-52][test/browser-specific/esm.spec.js:7-9]  
The repository uses Playwright for browser tests, and those tests require the generated browser bundle. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:35-47][AGENTS.md:87-92]  
Run `npm run test-node:unit` for unit tests, `npm run test-node:integration` for integration tests, `npm run test-node:interfaces` for interface tests, `npm run test-node:reporters` for reporter tests, and `npm run test-browser` for browser tests. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:35-47]  
The integration command builds before running parallel integration tests, while the browser command cleans and builds before invoking Playwright. [package.json]  
Tests commonly use `describe`, `it`, `test`, lifecycle hooks such as `beforeEach` and `afterEach`, and assertion or mocking libraries including Chai, Unexpected, and Sinon. [test/integration/fixtures/__default__.fixture.js:5-9][test/interfaces/qunit.spec.js:3-5][test/node-unit/buffered-worker-pool.spec.cjs:48-65][package.json]
